title: refactor: unify raw request URL logging
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces the configurable request-logger factory with one shared middleware and identical Gen/Enter re-exports.
- Intentionally keeps raw public URLs in Gen’s log context, including credential query parameters, matching Enter’s policy as requested. Request/response log emission remains local/test-only.
- Leaves structured error-input and realtime referrer telemetry redaction unchanged.
- Verifies singleton reuse, query order/encoding/duplicates, context, environment behavior, and adjacent tracking: 116 distinct targeted tests passed, plus both service typechecks, Biome 2.3.10, and whitespace checks.
- Follow-up to #14489; includes latest main. No deployment.

gist.headline: One log pipe, two hives
gist.blurb: Gen and Enter now share the same request logging middleware, so their raw URL notes travel through one well-tested little pipe.
gist.summary: Replaced separate configurable request-logger factories with a shared singleton middleware re-exported by both Gen and Enter, preserving raw public URL logging and existing error-input and realtime-referrer redaction behavior.
gist.impact: Developers get consistent Gen and Enter request-log context, including query ordering, encoding, and duplicate parameters, while local/test-only log emission and existing telemetry redaction remain intact.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared garden irrigation pipe connects two small retro terminal sheds labeled Gen and Enter; Polli, wearing a tiny plumber tool belt, checks that identical URL-shaped droplets flow through both pipes while sensitive telemetry notes remain safely tucked in sealed envelopes. Code-plants and flowers show the shared infrastructure growing cleanly.
